previous_text: Two objects X,Y in a 2-category are equivalent if there are 1-morphisms F:X→Y and G:Y→X with invertible 2-morphisms FG⇒id_Y and GF⇒id_X.
new_text: Two objects X,Y in a strict 2-category C are equivalent if there are 1-morphisms F:X→Y and G:Y→X together with invertible 2-morphisms F∘G⇒id_Y and G∘F⇒id_X. This is the Stacks Project strict 2-category convention; weak bicategory equivalences require a separate context/source review.
mathematical_reason: Stacks Section 4.29 explicitly declares it is defining strict 2-categories at the outset, and Definition 4.29.4 defines equivalent objects within that framework by 1-morphisms F,G and invertible 2-isomorphisms FG≈id and GF≈id. The inherited wording was mathematically plausible but lacked this source-specific qualification, making an unrestricted link to a strict 2-category over-general. The revised definition is deliberately restricted to the documented Stacks context; general bicategory/weak 2-category equivalence remains a separate unscreened variant research need.
